summary:
To the Moon... A Different Perspective is an interactive web application designed to explore the lunar environment and support the understanding of challenges associated with future human exploration.
Users can select different lunar locations and dates to visualize the apparent positions of the Earth and the Sun from the lunar surface, tracking their altitude and azimuth over time. The application simulates a complete lunar day, helping users understand sunlight availability and changing lighting conditions.
It also features a solar energy estimation module that calculates the potential power output and accumulated energy of solar panels on the Moon. Users can customize parameters such as panel area, efficiency, tilt, orientation, and system losses.
Whenever available, the application integrates astronomical data from NASA/JPL Horizons, complemented by local estimations.
Our goal is to make lunar environmental conditions easier to understand and demonstrate how astronomical data and renewable energy technologies can contribute to sustainable lunar exploration.
By combining interactive visualization, astronomical simulation, and solar energy calculations, our project helps investigate where and when solar energy can be generated, supporting the planning of future lunar bases and a sustainable human presence beyond Earth.
details:
To the Moon... A Different Perspective is an interactive web application designed to explore the lunar environment and understand the challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon.

Users can select predefined lunar locations or enter custom coordinates and dates to visualize the apparent positions of the Earth and the Sun from the lunar surface. The application displays their altitude and azimuth and includes a time simulation to explore how these positions and lighting conditions change throughout a lunar day.

It also features a solar energy estimation module that calculates the potential power output and accumulated energy of solar panels installed on the Moon. Users can customize parameters such as panel area, photovoltaic efficiency, tilt, orientation and system losses.

Whenever available, real time astronomical data from NASA/JPL Horizons is integrated, complemented by a local estimation alternative.

Our project's creativity lies in combining astronomical visualization, time simulation and renewable energy estimation into a single interactive platform.

Instead of simply presenting scientific data, we allow users to experience the lunar environment from a different perspective: that of an observer standing on the Moon. This makes it possible to connect astronomical phenomena with practical challenges, such as determining when and where solar energy could be generated.

During development, we considered lunar geography, day-night cycles, sunlight availability, solar panel orientation and efficiency, astronomical accuracy, and user accessibility. We also prioritized an intuitive interface that makes scientific information understandable without requiring advanced technical knowledge.

We recognize that energy calculations are estimates based on simplified assumptions and are intended for educational exploration rather than certified engineering design.

Our vision is to help people see the Moon not just as a destination, but as a place where humanity could one day live, work and build a sustainable future.
